title: Jonah and the Playlist
premise: Rafael Galloway, a closeted baker's kid who channels everything he can't say into his bread, finds his late grandmother's recipe box hiding instructions that have nothing to do with food — a coded playlist of tasks, confessions, and warnings left by a woman who survived something the family never talks about. Following her directions drags him into a school-wide baking championship he never wanted, a fragile romance with debate-team captain Jonah Adeyemi, and a family secret about what grandma gave up to keep the bakery alive. When the championship and the playlist's final task collide the same week as graduation, Rafael must choose between the safe, invisible life his family built and the visible, costly one grandma's legacy demands — and he wins neither trophy he was supposed to win, but keeps the bakery, the boy, and finally his own name.
about_author: Paloma Oyelaran is a former bakery counter girl from Lagos-by-way-of-Leeds who writes warm, hungry stories about queer kids and the families that almost understand them. She still measures her feelings in cups and spoons.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A late shift at Galloway's Bakery: Rafael bakes his anxiety over graduation and a crush he's never named into a batch of cardamom rolls nobody orders. Establishes his invisibility as armor. Beat: quiet ache, the comfort of routine about to crack.

chapters.title: The Box That Isn't a Box
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Sorting grandma's things, he finds a recipe card titled 'For When You Can't Stay Small' with directions to a hidden compartment and a cassette labeled only 'Track One.' His mother shuts the conversation down fast. Beat: curiosity vs. family silence.

chapters.title: Track One: Feed Someone the Truth
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The first playlist task: bake something honest and give it to someone who scares you. He hands a roll to Jonah Adeyemi, who tastes it and says, 'Okay, who hurt you?' Beat: terrified exhilaration of being seen.

chapters.title: Entry Forms and Other Lies
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah, needing a partner for the district Baking Championship to pad his college applications, recruits Rafael. Rafael says yes for reasons he won't examine. Beat: the deal that binds them, disguised as convenience.

chapters.title: Track Two: Learn What She Gave Up
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Task two sends him to the county archives, where he finds grandma's name on a 1970s lawsuit she withdrew — a discrimination case against the bakery's old landlord. His mother refuses to explain. Beat: the first hard edge of inheritance.

chapters.title: Flour Fight, Real Feelings
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Championship practice in the closed bakery after hours turns into a flour-dusted near-kiss interrupted by Rafael's dad coming downstairs. Beat: warmth and panic in equal measure.

chapters.title: Track Three: Sing Where They Can Hear
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The task requires doing something public and unhidden. Rafael enters the open-mic with a poem about bread and his grandmother; half the school films it. Beat: exposure — thrilling and dangerous.

chapters.title: Prelims: Burnt Sugar
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Preliminary round: their entry is good but Rafael freezes when his parents appear in the crowd, and they scrape through on Jonah's improvisation. Jonah starts asking questions Rafael won't answer. Beat: first real friction.

chapters.title: What Mom Knows
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Confrontation: his mother admits grandma walked away from the lawsuit to protect the family, traded her name for the bakery's survival — and warns Rafael that being visible has a price. Beat: love expressed as fear.

chapters.title: Track Four: The Person You're Avoiding
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Task four: make amends with someone you've hurt. It points, uncomfortably, at Jonah — Rafael has been pulling away since the near-kiss. Beat: guilt, and the courage to knock on a door.

chapters.title: Jonah's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah's home, his own pressures — a family that expects perfection, no room for softness. He and Rafael actually talk; Rafael comes out to him. Beat: intimacy earned through honesty.

chapters.title: Semifinals: The Recipe That Isn't Ours
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A rival team's entry is suspiciously close to a Galloway signature — grandma's stolen recipe, leaked years ago. Rafael's anger sharpens the semifinal bake into something fierce. They advance. Beat: righteous fire.

chapters.title: Track Five: Ask Her Why
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The task leads to grandma's old friend, who reveals the full story: grandma was outed in 1974, lost her own love, and folded it all into the playlist for whichever grandkid needed it. Beat: grief and gratitude braided together.

chapters.title: Outed Before He's Ready
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A classmate posts the open-mic video with a caption that outs Rafael to the whole school. His parents find out from a group chat, not from him. Beat: the floor drops out; the price of visibility arrives.

chapters.title: Closed Sign
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Rafael goes dark — no texts, no practice, bakery shuttered for 'family reasons.' Jonah shows up anyway and gets turned away at the door by Rafael's father. Beat: helplessness on both sides of the glass.

chapters.title: The Long Proof
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Days of silence at home; dad won't speak, mom defends grandma's compromise, Rafael refuses to inherit silence as a legacy. He starts baking again at 3 a.m., alone, for no one. Beat: rock bottom that is also a beginning.

chapters.title: Track Six: Finish What She Started
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The final task: refile what grandma withdrew. Rafael finds the old case documents and a letter — grandma's own unfinished coming-out, addressed 'to the one who bakes like me.' Beat: inheritance redefined; duty and love reconciled.

chapters.title: Finals: Everything in the Case
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Championship final. Rafael shows up with a bake that is openly, unmistakably about being queer and a Galloway — and loses first place to the rivals on a technicality. Jonah holds his hand in front of everyone. Beat: losing the trophy that doesn't matter.

chapters.title: The Championship That Does
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael presents the reopened case and grandma's letter at the bakery's lease hearing, publicly claiming the story — and his name. The community response splits the family but saves the shop. Beat: the real victory, won at cost.

chapters.title: Bread for the Table
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Graduation week: dad, wordlessly, sets out Rafael's cardamom rolls at the family table — an olive branch in his only language. Jonah and Rafael make plans that assume a future. Beat: tentative, earned reconciliation.

chapters.title: Track Seven: Stay
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The playlist's last card is blank except for one word: 'Stay.' Rafael adds his own card to the box — his recipe, his truth, for whoever comes next — and chooses to stay visible. Beat: quiet resolution, legacy continued.

chapters.title: Galloway's, Open
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Epilogue: summer at the reopened bakery, a small plaque for grandma, Rafael and Jonah running the counter together, the championship trophy conspicuously absent and nobody missing it. Beat: warmth, fullness, the price paid and worth it.
